brief: CXMT's claimed progress on a new 4F² DRAM architecture threatens Samsung and SK Hynix's lead, triggering a sharp memory and AI-semiconductor selloff: Goldman's Memory and AI Semiconductor baskets fell 9.3% and 6.7% during October 5-12, and the Memory basket now sits 25% below its June peak though still more than triple year-ago levels. Goldman's Robert Quinn traces the damage through Nasdaq futures positioning. Leveraged longs kept paying up to hold Nasdaq exposure even as memory fell, then that funding premium rolled over on October 12's selling. CFTC data show the "Other" (fast-money) category's Nasdaq futures gross longs hit one-year highs in both notional and open-interest terms on October 6, one day before the OpenAI revenue scare and five days before CXMT's announcement, meaning those longs are now underwater. Asset Manager gross longs, by contrast, remain near their June record and show no reaction yet. Quinn calls that disconnect "debatable"; Goldman's desks still expect the broader dip to be bought, with ASML and TSMC earnings as the first tests, but frame the still-high asset-manager length as the larger unresolved risk.
